terms.gloss: intransitive, neither active nor passive (of verbs)
terms.comment: verba neutra are verbs that are neither active nor passive, such as sedeō, stō, cubō (Traupman 228); Lewis & Short also cites Cic. Or. 155 for the usage.
Traupman’s verbum neutrāle. Lewis & Short gives neutrālis only of the neuter gender (Quintilian); we have found no ancient instance of it for verbs.

phrases.latin: Dā exempla verbī neutrālis. — Sedeō, stō, cubō.
phrases.english: Give some examples of an intransitive verb. — I sit, I stand, I lie.

sources: Lewis & Short: neuter · Lewis & Short: intransitivus · Lewis & Short: neutralis
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 227, p. 228, p. 244, p. 247.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
